## Contact Information
For questions regarding this report, please contact Matthew Saponaro, Ph.D., Director of the [Technology Service Center](https://www.sites.udel.edu/technology-service-center) at University of Delaware

## Motivation

The purpose of this inventory is to identify, measure, and document large, mature trees in Rittenhouse Park. The collected data will support planning, maintenance, ecological assessments, and long-term urban forestry initiatives. Redd Park Trail will be addressed separately rather than compared directly with Rittenhouse Park.

## Overview

In the current Rittenhouse Park inventory, 55 trees were inventoried. All 55 are currently classified as large mature trees. Based on DBH measurements, 51 trees meet the DBH threshold of 20 inches or greater, while 4 trees fall below that threshold but were still recorded during field collection. See Figure [6](inventoryInsights.html#tree-type-distribution-across-sites) for more details. In this project, "significant trees" were defined as follows:

-   **Large mature trees**: Any trees with a Diameter at Breast height (DBH) ≥ 20 inches
-   **Young tree**: Young, intentionally planted trees that have reached a stage of growth where supplemental support is no longer present
-   **Newly planted trees**: Young, intentionally planted trees with supplemental support (e.g., wooden stakes or protective cages)

## Inventoried Locations

We collected the current report data in Rittenhouse Park under the site code RH-P. The inventory focused on trees located within the park and near the trail area so that trees with potential maintenance, canopy, or safety relevance could be documented consistently.

Redd Park Trail will be addressed separately. In the narrative, it should be described as Redd Park Trail. For broader trail context and mapping, see the [Delaware Greenways interactive trail map](https://delawaregreenways.org/trail-library/).
